shipped_rows.title_o: When more is less: A counterintuitive effect of distractor frequency in the picture-word interference paradigm.

blind_target.title: Now you see it, now you don’t: On turning semantic interference into facilitation in a Stroop-like task.
blind_target.evidence_quote: To ensure that distractors were processed under masked conditions, we used the same time parameters as Finkbeiner and Caramazza (2006), and also included control conditions in which picture and distractor were either semantically related or unrelated. If distractors are processed, semantic facilitation should be found in the masked condition and semantic interference in the visible condition.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Also, the same semantic facilitation effect was found by Finkbeiner & Caramazza (2006) who used the same presentation parameters as we did.

luna_triage.reason: Experiment 2 tested semantic facilitation in the masked condition, and the discussion explicitly compares its result with the same effect reported by Finkbeiner and Caramazza (2006). The reference list identifies the 2006 Cortex article. Supplied row 663 is Miozzo and Caramazza (2003), the separate source of the distractor-frequency effect, and does not represent the 2006 original.
